subject: log-details
text:
- `process-exit` exit 1: `already-live` (a `live` or a `stale` holder of the name, from `viola run` or from `viola revive`, which prints `run`'s own collision pair, or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"already-live","detail":null}` document — revive's preflight refusals under `--json` are the same-shaped document with their code, the logged line unchanged (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract); a `gone` holder is taken over with no exit-1 line), `squatted-name`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `batch-script-child`, `internal-error`, and from `viola revive`'s start-arm preflight `no-session` (no logged session, or an `--id` the log does not hold), `session-live` (one `claude agents --json` read lists the logged session id live in another `claude`; skipped under `--fork`; a failed, oversize or malformed read passes, fail open; chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) and `cwd-missing` (the snapshot records no directory, or one that is not an existing directory). The preflight reads the holder, then the session, then `session-live`, then the directory, and takes no later reading once one refuses; each refusal is one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in `run-<name>.ndjson` with no child started. `strict-modes-failed` is no longer one of them (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor): the start arm's instance check (`check_instance`) runs before the wrapper log opens and outside the preflight, so its refusal is the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair (or under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) and exit 1 with no log opened, no `process-start`, no `process-exit` and no child.
 And `interrupted`: a `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Break) before its rows are checked ends with one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` in `cli-<name>.ndjson` under a `VIOLA_NAME` (no file with no instance, D-06), after every spawn pair it opened is closed (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes the `process-exit` `detail` at 13 values (the enum's members; 12 before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, 11 before chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup, 9 before chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive).

subject: log-details
text:
- `hook-decision` fail-open codes (security Vector 4): `oversize-stdin`, `malformed-json`, `channel-unreachable`, `server-verify-failed`, `strict-modes-failed`, `unverified-cli`, `deadline`. `viola hook statusline` uses three of the seven (the rule: the `detail` codes the arm's fail-open paths write): `oversize-stdin`, `malformed-json`, and `deadline`, which on that arm is the 5 s PROVISIONAL bound on the user's command, not a dialog deadline. Its refused instance check writes no `hook-decision` and no other line (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; before it the arm wrote `strict-modes-failed`, four of the seven).
 `server-verify-failed` is written by `viola hook` on a server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made (Linux and Windows): `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN into `hook-<name>.ndjson`; on the dialog path the order is `hook-invoked{corr:null}` then `hook-decision{corr:null, decision_emitted:false, detail:"server-verify-failed"}`.

subject: log-details
text:
- Filesystem refusals (Vector 7): `strict-modes-failed` (on `process-exit` exit 21, and on `parse-rejected{parser:"ledger-stamps"}` from `run`'s version gate, at `warn`, with no path; `viola revive`'s start arm and `viola revive --list` both refuse on `viola_state::strict::check_instance` with the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document, exit 1 and no log line; on `hook-decision` the schema's `detail` enum keeps the word and no arm writes it, since `viola hook statusline`'s refused check leaves no line and the nine hook events run no instance check; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `viola list`'s refused scan of the home, `instances/` or an instance exits 21 on both forms and writes no line either — no `process-start`, no `process-exit`, no `strict-modes-failed` — so on `process-exit` exit 21 no arm of this build writes the word; chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; `viola plugin install`'s refused `check_path` of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir exits 21 and writes no line either, under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document (chunk 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install); `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused `check_instance` of the driven instance exits 21 and writes no line either — no `process-start`, no `process-exit` — the fixed instance-state pair on stderr, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), `pinned-hash-mismatch` (on `process-exit` exit 1), `symlink-ignored`. A skipped symlink has no exit or decision to carry it. The `viola-state` call site that skips a symlinked entry therefore emits `parse-rejected{parser:"state-entry", detail:"symlink-ignored", count}` once per scan, at `warn`, into the scanning process's role file. The entry name and the link target are never logged.
 As landed its call site is `viola_state::board::read` (`viola list`, chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): after its loop, one `parse-rejected{parser:"state-entry", detail:"symlink-ignored"|"malformed", count}` per nonzero count of `board::scan` (links ignored; a non-directory or a name that is no `ViolaName`), naming no entry, into `cli-<name>.ndjson` under a `VIOLA_NAME` for `viola list`, and into `mcp.ndjson` for `viola mcp`'s `list` tool (through `list::board_document`, chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); `board::scan` itself counts and logs nothing.

subject: errors
text: - When an instance resolves, it also writes `{"event":"panic", ..., "panic_payload":"<escaped>", "backtrace":[...frames]}` as one line to `detail-<process>.ndjson`. The backtrace is raw, never-symbolised frames from `src/panic_frames.rs` — `RtlCaptureStackBackTrace` + `GetModuleHandleExW`/`GetModuleFileNameW` on Windows, `libc::backtrace` + `dladdr` on Unix — up to 62 strings `0x<ip> <module path> base=0x<base> +0x<offset>` (or `0x<ip> ?`), enough for an offline resolver against the pinned copy. It is **not** gated by `RUST_BACKTRACE`, because env vars are not a configuration channel. Symbolising in the panic path was retired: `Backtrace::force_capture().to_string()` cost 351.4 ms of a 402.7 ms hook run for 72 frames on the Windows runner and pushed the forced-panic hook to 1.50 s against the 1.0 s spine bound; the raw capture measured 23.7 ms (as measured at chunk 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify, CI runs 36436266196, 36435153705 and 36448654074).

subject: errors
text:
- The panic hook only writes. The exit is decided at a catch site:
  - **Main-thread catch site (every role):** everything after `set_hook` (clap parse, init and role dispatch) runs inside one `std::panic::catch_unwind` in the root bin's `main`. An `Err` maps to the role's exit below, so no role ends through an uncaught unwind (Rust's default exit 101). The role is taken from argv before clap runs: the first argument that is neither a global flag nor a flag's value (for example `--home <path>`) and that names a role subcommand (`run`, `hook`, `mcp`; `role_of` in `src/main.rs` names `revive` beside `run`, except `revive` followed (after any `--home` pair) by `--list` before a `--`, which is `cli`; a `--list` after `--` is the child's word; any other verb is `cli`). `viola revive`'s start arm logs as process `run` (the `run-<name>.ndjson` role file and `run`'s detail sink), opened by the log setup it shares with `run` only after its instance check has passed; a refused check on the start arm is the stderr pair and exit 1 with no process log opened. `viola revive <name> --list` is `cli`, so its dispatch `Err` or panic reaches the `cli` catch site (`process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}`, exactly `error: internal error`); its refused strict-modes check opens no log and writes no line (the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document, exit 1), and its `no-session` is `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail:"no-session"}` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson` under a name, with the stderr pair or the `no-session` document (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract). So `viola --home <dir> hook stop` is still a `hook`, and a pre-init panic in it still exits 0. Reading `argv[1]` alone would misclassify that form as `cli` and exit 1 (D-28).
  - **`run` worker threads:** the PTY pump and handle-wait thread bodies each run inside `catch_unwind`. An `Err` is sent to `main`, which takes the `run` exit path below, because the session cannot continue without either thread. A worker panic that leaves `main` running with no `process-exit` is forbidden. A panic in one channel server connection worker is contained: the `channel.dispatch` `Drop` guard logs `channel-response{result_class:"error", error_code:-32603}`, the connection closes, and `run` continues. The vt100 feed thread (`src/run/gate.rs`, detached) is contained too: its `catch_unwind` wraps each feed and resize, a caught panic poisons the screen model and writes one `parse-rejected`, nothing is sent to `main`, and `run` continues; the ban above covers the PTY pump and the handle-wait thread.
  - **Unwinding is required:** every Cargo profile keeps `panic = "unwind"`. `panic = "abort"` turns every `catch_unwind` into an abort, so `hook` would die by SIGABRT instead of exiting 0. Gate G3 (§9) enforces this.

subject: errors
text: - Before step 4 of init, no file exists, so the panic hook writes nothing. This window contains clap parsing and home resolution, and the instance check that `viola revive`'s start arm and `viola hook statusline` run before any role file is opened (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola mcp`'s check of its home and `diagnostics/`, also run before any role file is opened (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), and the instance check that `viola link` / `viola unlink` run on the driven instance before their `cli` role file opens, whose refusal (exit 21 `instance-unreachable`: the fixed instance-state pair, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`) writes no line in any log and leaves the directory's mode as found.

subject: errors
text: - vt100 panics are caught on `run`'s feed thread (`src/run/gate.rs`) by a `catch_unwind` around each feed and resize, not inside `run.readiness_gate`. Each poisoning episode gives exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed", count:1}` at `WARN` with no `corr`, its `detail` set by the cause: `panicked` for a caught vt100 panic, `oversize` for a copy the bounded feed queue dropped (a size message carries the drop count at its offer, so a drop after a queued resize poisons the fresh screen again). The model stays poisoned until the host size changes, and `run` continues. `viola_panic_hook` runs before the catch returns, so a panic poisoning also writes the hook's `event:"panic"` role line and its detail line. Witnessed at run level by `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` (chunk 2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records): exactly one `parse-rejected{vt100-feed, panicked}` and one `event:"panic"` line, both asserted present, then `viola send` refused `send-refused{detail:"input-not-ready"}` (exit 13) while a typed key still reaches the child. G2's single seam exemption is unchanged: that test's home lives outside `target/e2e-home` (`TestHome::outside_scan()`), so G2, G4 and the secret scan do not read it (the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer).

subject: slo-gates
text:
- **Zero unlogged panics:** every panic in `run`, `hook`, `mcp` and `cli` **after init step 4** produces **exactly one** single-line `level:"ERROR", event:"panic"` record in its home-level role file, with no multi-line backtrace in home-level files, and `hook` still exits 0. Retry-once policies for panic handling are forbidden, in parallel with the tests' `retries = 0`.
  - **Counting rule:** "exactly one", the `viola.panic` counter and gate G2 (§9) count home-level role files only. G2 alone also leaves out the `fake-agent` seam's deliberate panic (a `panic_location` of exactly `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs:<digits>`, §9): that line is still written exactly once — the invariant holds for it — and only its count is exempt. The companion line in `detail-<process>.ndjson` also carries `event:"panic"` and is excluded. In merged `agent-run logs` output, count `select(.record.event=="panic" and (.file|startswith("detail-")|not))`.
  - **Bounded exemptions** (no file exists, so no line can be written):
    1. the pre-init window before step 4 (§7: clap parse and home resolution, the instance check of both `viola revive` arms (the start arm and `--list`, whose check runs before its `cli` role file opens) and of `viola hook statusline`, and `viola list`'s strict-modes scan, which runs before its `cli` role file opens, and `viola mcp`'s check of its home and `diagnostics/`, which runs before its `mcp` role file opens, chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, and `viola plugin install`'s check of its home and `marketplace/` tree dirs, which runs before its `cli` role file opens, and the instance check of `viola link` / `viola unlink` on the driven instance, which runs before their `cli` role file opens);
    2. `cli` without a resolved instance (D-06);
    3. `hook` without `VIOLA_NAME` (D-16);
    4. a failed step-4 role-file open (§3 init step 4). The writer becomes `std::io::sink`, or stderr JSON for `mcp` (D-09), and the panic hook's `OnceLock` stays empty, so it writes nothing, not even to `mcp`'s stderr (D-32).
    5. the hidden capture arms, `hook <event> --capture` and `hook statusline --capture` (which runs no instance check and no pass-through), each doing no obs init and so having no role file; a panic there writes no line and the hook still exits 0, as in exemption 3.
    6. (retired, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract: `viola revive <name> --list` opens the `cli` role log under a `VIOLA_NAME` once its check has passed, so a panic there writes its one line; with no `VIOLA_NAME` it is exemption 2, and its refused check is exemption 7. The number is kept so the others keep theirs.) `viola revive`'s start arm is not exempt once its instance check has passed: its role file is then `run-<name>.ndjson`.
    7. a refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`) or on `viola hook statusline` (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), or a refused `viola list` scan of the home, `instances/` or an instance (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list, the operator's answer at its planning), or `viola mcp`'s refused check of its home or `diagnostics/` through `viola_state::strict::check_path` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, its plan's lean, approved by the operator at P5), or `viola plugin install`'s refused check of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir through `check_path` (chunk 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install), or a refused `check_instance` of the driven instance on `viola link` / `viola unlink`: it opens no role file and writes no line (revive: the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document, and exit 1; statusline: exit 0 and nothing printed; list and plugin install: exit 21, the `--json` error document or the stderr pair; link and unlink: exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document; mcp: exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr), so a panic there writes none, by §7's rule; no forced-panic case reads it. That a refused check writes no line on `viola hook statusline` and on `viola list` is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at those chunks' planning, superseded 2026-10-13).

    The failure condition "a panic evidenced by an exit code without its line" applies only to processes whose `process-start` is in a home-level role file. For the exemptions the only evidence is the exit status. `hook` still exits 0, so a D-16 panic is unobservable by design (E1).

subject: logs
text: - NEVER use `print!` / `println!` / `eprint!` / `eprintln!` / `dbg!` in the `hook`, `run` or `mcp` code paths of the product crates (`viola-harness` and the fake agent are exempt, §3 obs-ci-gate-wire). They bypass the file sink and break the Hook contract, the `run` terminal rule and MCP framing. Enforced by `[workspace.lints.clippy]` `print_stdout`, `print_stderr`, `dbg_macro` = `deny` under the §9 clippy step. Only the output modules that own `--json`, human CLI stderr and the hook decision body may carry a local `#[allow]`, and only where they use a print macro — `run`'s and `revive`'s pre-spawn refusals, `revive --list`'s, `verify`'s, `list`'s and `plugin install`'s refusals, and `link`'s / `unlink`'s instance-check refusal, write through `src/human.rs` (`refuse` / `write_refusal`, one `write_all` on the locked stderr; callers `run` 5 · `verify` 5 · `list` 2 · `revive` 1 · `plugin install` 1 · `link` 1, the one `link_call` site both verbs share; the rule: the `human::refuse(` call sites under `src/`), which uses no print macro and carries no `#[allow]` — plus the fake agent's crate-level `#![allow]` in `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (a root-package bin, §3 obs-ci-gate-wire).
